blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Delivery scheduling is about promises. When you tell a customer "your order will arrive tomorrow between 10 and 12", you make a time window. This is a small promise. Now the whole team has to keep it.

Time windows and SLAs are how companies commit to customers. A missed window is not just a late parcel. It is a broken promise. Over time, broken promises become lost customers.

Good scheduling protects promises that the team can really keep. It does not promise windows that only look good on a website. A realistic promise is better than a nice-looking one.

items.q: What is a time window?
options: A small promise about when the order will arrive
items.why: "you make a time window. This is a small promise."

items.q: According to the text, a missed window is…
items.why: "A missed window is not just a late parcel. It is a broken promise."

items.q: What happens over time when promises are broken?
items.why: "Over time, broken promises become lost customers."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: Promise only what the team can really do
A realistic promise is a good promise
Promise the fastest window to look good on the website
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que promessas bonitas no site, mas impossíveis, são ruins.

items.q: The text suggests that a promise is only good if…
options: it looks nice on the website
the team can really keep it
items.why: Inferência: "Good scheduling protects promises that the team can really keep."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie treinando um novo programador de entregas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, welcome to the team. Today I want to talk about time windows. It is the most important part of your new job.

When you plan a delivery, you make a promise to the customer. You say the parcel will arrive between ten and twelve. That is a small promise, but it is a real one. The driver, the warehouse and the customer all depend on it.

Here is the mistake many new schedulers make. They want to look fast, so they promise a very tight window. Two hours. One hour. It looks great on the screen. But if the team cannot keep it, the promise breaks. And a broken promise is expensive. You do not lose one parcel. Over time, you lose the customer.

So my advice is simple. Be realistic, not optimistic. Promise a window you can really keep. And one more tip: call the customer fifteen minutes before you arrive. It sounds small, but it stops a lot of failed deliveries. We will review the missed windows every week and look for the pattern. Okay? Let's start.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie say is the most important part of the new job?
items.why: "Today I want to talk about time windows. It is the most important part of your new job."

items.q: What mistake do many new schedulers make?
options: They call the customer too much
They promise a very tight window to look fast
items.why: "they want to look fast, so they promise a very tight window."

items.q: What tip does Sophie give about the customer?
options: Send an email in the morning
Call fifteen minutes before you arrive
Ask the customer to wait at home all day
items.why: "call the customer fifteen minutes before you arrive."

items.q: Why does Sophie say a broken promise is "expensive"?
options: You can lose the customer, not just one parcel
items.why: Inferência: "You do not lose one parcel. Over time, you lose the customer."

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "be realistic, not optimistic"?
options: Promise a window you can really keep
items.why: Inferência: ser realista = prometer só o que dá para cumprir, não o que parece bom.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A time window tells the customer when the parcel will arrive." A time window is…
options: a period when delivery will happen
items.why: Time window = janela de entrega, o período em que a entrega deve acontecer.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We must ___ the promise we made to the customer."
items.why: To keep a promise = cumprir a promessa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The plan must be ___, not just nice on the website."
items.why: Realistic = realista: possível de cumprir de verdade.

items.q: "An SLA is a service level agreement." It is…
options: a formal promise about the service, with consequences
items.why: SLA = nível de serviço: um compromisso formal com o cliente.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If we miss the window, we can get a ___."
items.why: Lost customer = cliente perdido, o resultado de quebrar promessas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem no trabalho de logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Can you set up the delivery for tomorrow?" To set up means to…
items.why: Set up = organizar, preparar algo.

items.q: "We will roll out the new schedule next week." To roll out means to…
options: start using it, step by step
items.why: Roll out = colocar em prática aos poucos.

items.q: "The customer pushed back on the late window." This means the customer…
options: was not happy and said no
items.why: Push back on = resistir, não concordar com algo.

items.q: "We said we would call, and we followed through." This means we…
items.why: Follow through = fazer até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A quick call before delivery can make a difference." This means it can…
items.why: Make a difference = fazer diferença de verdade, mudar o resultado.
